chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah bin Yahya al-Kahili, from Minhal al-Qassab, who said:
I said to him, 'What is the limit of al-talaaqee?' He said, 'Rawha.'

key_terms.التَّلَقِّي: Receiving goods from the caravan before they enter the city market
key_terms.رَوْحَةٌ: A specific distance unit (four farsakhs) used as a legal boundary in trade

ai.seo_question: What is the legal definition and distance of Rawha for receiving goods outside the city?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Ibn Mahbub transmits the definition of 'Rawha' as the precise legal threshold for 'al-talaaqee', where merchants intercept caravans outside the city limits to secure goods before they reach the main market. This definition is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between permissible early purchase and the prohibited practice of 'kaff al-talaaqee' (withholding goods from the general populace), thereby ensuring market fairness and transparency in trade transactions.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Yahya Al Kahily, from Minhal Al Qassab who said,
‘I said to himasws, ‘What is the limit of the receipt of trade outside the city?’ Heasws said: ‘A Rawha (four Fasakhs – about six miles)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Yahya al-Kahily from Minhal al-Qassab who has said the following: “

I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘What is the limit of going out to meet a caravan of suppliers?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is a distance of one Rawhah (four Farasikh which is equal to six miles)”’
